title: NCAA College Football 2026-27: Here’s Where to Watch Games Live Online for Free
summary: Livestream games for weekends full of college football action starting Saturday (Aug. 29) — watch online free.
contentText:

If Sundays are for NFL games, Saturdays are for 2026 NCAA College Football. The top-ranked teams, like Ohio State Buckeyes, Oregon Ducks, Georgia Bulldogs, Indiana Hoosiers and more, throughout the country compete for glory to the win the 2027 College Football Playoff Championship at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas at the end of the season.

How to Watch NCAA College Football 2026-27 Season Online, at a Glance:

- Date: Aug. 29-Jan. 25, 2027

- Network: ABC, ACC Network, Big Ten Network, CBS, CBS Sports Network, The CW, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, FOX, FS1, FS2, NBC, SEC Network, TBS, TNT and truTV

- Online Streaming: DirecTV , Fubo , Hulu + Live TV , Sling TV , ESPN Unlimited , Paramount+ , FOX One , Peacock , HBO Max

Watch on DirecTV

When Does the 2026-27 NCAA Football Season Start ?

The NCAA Football season starts Saturday, Aug. 29 with the North Carolina Tar Heels taking on the TCU Horned Frogs at Aviva Stadium in Dublin, Ireland, with a start time of noon ET/9 a.m. PT. Check out a complete NCAA Football schedule here .

What TV Networks Feature the 2026-27 NCAA Football Season?

NCAA college football games broadcast across multiple networks, including ABC, ACC Network, Big Ten Network, CBS, CBS Sports Network, The CW, ESPN , ESPN2, ESPNU, FOX, FS1, FS2, NBC, SEC Network, TBS, TNT and truTV.

Meanwhile, games are available to livestream on ESPN Unlimited, Paramount+, FOX One, Peacock and HBO Max.

Where to Watch the 2026-27 NCAA Football Season Online for Free

For cord-cutters, there are a few ways to watch college football, if you don’t have cable, especially if you want to watch for free. DirecTV has a five-day free trial , while other streaming services, such as Fubo and Hulu + Live TV , also offer free trials, so you can watch games for free.

EDITOR'S PICK

DirecTV

Get 5-Day Free Trial

Comes with a five-day free trial.

600+ FREE CHANNELS

Sling TV

Get Sling TV

Sling Orange & Blue comes with 50+ broadcast and cable channels.

Sling TV offers the Orange & Blue plan, which comes with ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, FOX, FS1, FS2, NBC, TBS, TNT and truTV. With more than 50 channels, the streaming plan goes for $69.99 per month. For For games on ACC Network, Big Ten Network and SEC Network, you’d have to add Sling Sports Extra starting at an additional $11 per month. All plans come with a free cloud DVR and an extra 600 or so free channels too. Please note: Pricing and channel availability vary from market-to-market.

UNLIMITED DVR

FuboTV

NO HIDDEN FEES

Hulu + Live TV

Get 3-day free trial

Comes with Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Unlimited.

Broadcast and cable networks ABC, ACC Network, Big Ten Network, CBS, CBS Sports Network, The CW, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, FOX, FS1, FS2, NBC, SEC Network, TBS, TNT and truTV are all available to watch with Hulu + Live TV . Prices for the cable alternative start at $89.99 per month for more than 100 live channels, while each plan comes with Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Unlimited at no additional cost. Hulu + Live TV might be best for those who want all of these streaming services together in one package.

INCLUDES CW SPORTS

ESPN Unlimited

Get espn unlimited here

Comes with all things ESPN.

ESPN Unlimited is the official streaming platform for ESPN. A subscription includes instant access for $29.99 per month. However, you can save almost 17% off by purchasing an annual subscription for $299.99 per year. It features every ESPN network, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, SEC Network+ and ACC Network Extra — all in one streaming service. It even comes with CW Sports for more livestream games.

In addition to live sports, ESPN Unlimited has original programming to stream on demand. Although the service doesn’t offer a free trial, you can still watch ESPN Unlimited with a clever workaround to watch online for free. Learn more about how to get a free trial to access ESPN Unlimited here .

STREAM ON 3 DEVICES AT ONCE

Paramount+

Get Paramount+

There are two plans to choose from: Paramount+ Essential and Paramount+ Premium (with Showtime).

Paramount+ has NCAA College Football games on CBS and CBS Sports streaming online, as well as past seasons. If you don’t already have a Paramount+ subscription, the streaming service plan goes for $8.99 per month (or $89.99 per year). With Paramount+ , you’ll get access to a wide selection of TV shows and movies, live sports, 24-hour news with CBS News and more.

ALL THINGS FOX

FOX One

Prime Video Channel add-on.

With prices starting at $19.99 per month, FOX One is your one-stop app for everything FOX has to offer, including streaming access to NCAA College Football games on FOX, FS1, FS2 and Big Ten Network. It also includes FOX News, FOX Business, FOX Nation, FOX Weather, FOX Deportes and your local FOX broadcasting affiliate.

Prime Video has a three-day free trial available for Amazon Prime members, so you watch FOX One as an add-on to Amazon’s streaming service. Learn more about Prime Video and FOX One here .

THE OFFICIAL NBC STREAMER

Peacock

Get Peacock Premium

Starts at $10.99 per month.

There are two different plans offered on Peacock: The Premium Plan for $10.99 per month or the Premium Plus Plan for $16.99 per month. If you’re looking to save, you can get 17% off when you do the annual plan for $109.99 per year or $169.99 per year, respectively. With the Premium Plan, it’s ad-supported and you’ll receive access to a wide range of movies, TV shows, originals, live sports from NBC Sports and live news from NBC News.

Peacock’s Premium Plus plan comes with everything in the Premium plan , no ads, your local NBC channel live and the ability to download and stream offline.

HOME OF TNT SPORTS

HBO Max

Get HBO Max

Subscriptions start at $10.99 per month.

A subscription to HBO Max is the best way to watch NCAA College Football games on TNT, TBS and truTV online. The streaming service starts at $10.99 per month for the ad-supported plan. But you can get HBO Max bundled with Hulu and Disney+ starting at $19.99 per month for all three services.

More Ways to Watch

Moreover, college football games and events are known for celebrity sightings. Famous recording artists have been known to appear at games in the past, including Snoop Dogg, Kenny Chesney, Gucci Mane, Tobey Keith, Adam Duritz, Katy Perry, Darius Rucker and others.

Starting on Saturday (Aug. 29), the 2026-27 NCAA College Football season broadcast across on ABC, ACC Network, Big Ten Network, CBS, CBS Sports Network, The CW, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, FOX, FS1, FS2, NBC, SEC Network, TBS, TNT and truTV. One of the best ways to watch games is with DirecTV .
